newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cent lower Tuesday, although some traders expect the market to come in closer to unchanged following Monday's strong performance.

New York arabica futures charged higher yesterday, bolstered by speculative buying amid bullish technicals and concerns about tight nearby supply. September settled up 8.80 cents at an eight-week high of 193.75 cents a lb after ranging from 196.75 to 183.00 cents. December rose 6.40 cents to 168.70 cents, while the back months closed up 3.00 to 4.25.
The September/December switch, a barometer of near-term availability, bulged to 25.05 cents compared with 22.65 cents at the close on Friday.
On the charts, traders said September faces critical chart resistance at 198.00 cents, followed by 200.00 cents. Support was seen near 190.00 cents.
On the weather front, Weather Services Corp said Tuesday no damaging cold weather is expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 750 60-kg bags as of August 1, to 94,741 bags. An additional 4,429 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

Also late yesterday, the head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said Colombia will open registrations for September coffee exports next week once all August export commitments are fulfilled.

Jorge Cardenas also said Colombia would maintain its 30 U.S. cent quality premium on its international sales, contradicting market rumours that the premium could be cut to 20 cents to make the Colombian beans more competitive.

In other news, the International Coffee Organization (ICO) said producing members' exports reached 82.08 million 60-kg bags in the 12 months to June 1997, up from 73.18 million in the same 1996 period.
In June alone, exports fell to 5.87 million bags from 7.03 million in May. Exports in June 1996 totalled 5.88 million bags, ICO said.
London robusta futures were barely changed in listless trading early Tuesday. At the midday break, September was flat, at $1,660, after ranging from $1,675 to $1,655. November rose $2, to $1,657.
